questions.text: What distinguishes temporal grounding from simply recognizing that an event occurs in a video?

options.A: It identifies the event without needing any time information.
options.B: It localizes when the event occurs using timestamps or an interval.
options.C: It replaces video frames with one image-level semantic vector.
options.D: It predicts only the overall topic of the video.

questions.explanation: Temporal grounding associates an event with its time location, such as start and end timestamps, rather than only detecting its presence.

questions.text: To fit a video token budget, you can reduce sampled frames or pool each frame more. Which tradeoff is correct?

options.A: Fewer frames lose spatial detail; stronger spatial pooling loses temporal coverage.
options.B: Both changes preserve all event timing and all fine spatial detail.
options.C: Fewer frames increase temporal coverage; stronger pooling increases spatial detail.
options.D: Fewer frames risk missing brief events; stronger pooling risks losing fine spatial detail.

questions.explanation: Temporal subsampling can miss events between sampled frames. Spatial pooling compresses each frame and can obscure small objects or text.

questions.text: For a matching event name, predicted interval [2, 6] and ground-truth interval [4, 8] have what IoU, and do they pass tol_iou=0.3?
questions.explanation: Intersection length is 6−4=2; union spans 8−2=6. IoU=2/6=1/3, which is at least 0.3.
